title: Consultancy to Develop Learning Paper 2 for SPREAD- Integrating Peacebuilding, Livelihoods, Climate Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction
draft_excerpt:
Executive Summary

Dan Church Aid Kenya is commissioning this consultancy to develop Learning Paper 2 for SPREAD, Strengthening Integrated Peace, Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction for Cross-border Communities, implemented with TUPADO in Turkana/Kenya, ICPDO and ROG in Eastern Equatoria/South Sudan, and ECC in South Omo/Ethiopia. As SPREAD moves into its concluding phase after two years of implementation across the Karamoja Cluster, DCA needs an evidence base that establishes what "integration" has actually meant in practice, where combining peacebuilding, livelihoods, climate resilience and DRR interventions produced value beyond the sum of its parts, and where it did not. The assignment requires documentation of Community Action Groups, Village Savings and Loan Associations, community-based disaster risk reduction structures and observatory platforms alongside pre-existing market committees, peace committees and savings groups, drawing on direct engagement with pastoralists, agro-pastoralists, fisherfolk, farmers and farmer groups, formal and informal cross-border traders, women- and youth-led CSOs, traditional leaders and local and national authorities across all three countries. Cortech Consulting Group proposes to deliver the learning paper, the inception report, and the two distinct policy briefs specified in the Terms of Reference within the stated twelve-week window, addressing directly the criterion on which the Contracting Authority places the greatest weight: whether the Terms of Reference have been addressed in sufficient detail, at 20 of 100 points. Cortech's proposed approach treats the SPREAD assignment as a comparative learning exercise, not a standard evaluation. The design pairs deliberately selected stronger and weaker examples of integration across South Omo, Turkana and Eastern Equatoria, using the case-study method the ToR requires to explain why integrated programming worked better in some locations than others and to capture community preferences directly from CAG and VSLA members, traditional leaders and local authorities. Data collection is coordinated through the national partner teams, TUPADO, ICPDO, ROG and ECC, using harmonised KII and FGD tools rather than three separate national studies, so that findings are triangulated and comparable across borders and converge on a single cross-border validation workshop rather than dispersed national events. Sampling is built explicitly around the categories the ToR names: peacebuilding and resilience structures, livestock, fishing, farming, and formal and informal cross-border trade, spanning both women/youth-led and mixed markets, disaggregated by sex, age and disability. This design responds directly to the 20-point criterion on methodology and sampling adequacy and produces the two required policy briefs as distinct products from the outset, one on integration versus coordination for donors, IGAD and governments, the other on human security and regional stability for EU and Danish policymakers. The proposed team is led by Mugove Kwashirai Chakurira as Lead Consultant/Researcher, confirmed available for the full assignment period, responsible for the inception report, the learning paper, and both policy briefs. Edwin Aldrin Adenya is proposed as Research Assistant/Enumerator, positioned against the ToR's requirement that the consultant recruit and train research assistants for field-level KIIs, FGDs and community case-study data collection, and confirmed available across the fieldwork window. This gives the assignment full internal role coverage against the two personnel categories the ToR specifies, lead researcher and field-level research assistance, without reliance on personnel not yet confirmed. Cortech's relevant institutional experience includes the Research and Learning assignment for the Pathway to Prosperity Programme in Turkana West for the Danish Refugee Council (2025), which combined quantitative surveys with KIIs, FGDs and case studies under OECD-DAC-aligned learning objectives; the endline evaluation of the multi-sectoral peacebuilding and climate resilience project for the Lutheran World Federation in Somalia (2026), which applied a systems-thinking, nexus-oriented methodology treating peacebuilding and livelihoods as interconnected rather than siloed; and the CEWARN Regional Strategy Framework consultancy for the IGAD Secretariat (2024) across Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, South Sudan and Uganda, which produced policy-facing outputs on climate security integration for regional and national audiences. Delivery is sequenced against the dates DCA has fixed: inception report and tools by 13 October 2026, field data collection complete by 31 October, draft learning paper and both draft policy briefs to the Consortium Management Unit by 21 November, the single cross-border validation workshop on 3 December, and final learning paper, both final policy briefs, case-study files, the executive management summary and the summary presentation by 15 December 2026. Quality is controlled through CMU review at each draft stage and validation-workshop feedback incorporated before finalisation. Costs, daily rates and financial terms are addressed exclusively in the separate financial proposal submitted under Annex 2.

Subject: Consultancy to Develop Learning Paper 2 for SPREAD- Integrating Peacebuilding, Livelihoods, Climate Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction

Dear Mr. Bryan,

Cortech Consulting Group submits this technical proposal in response to Request for Proposal reference DCA/NBI/10/09/2026-2 for the consultancy to develop Learning Paper 2 under the SPREAD programme (Strengthening Integrated Peace, Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction for Cross-border Communities) across South Omo/Ethiopia, Turkana/Kenya and Eastern Equatoria/South Sudan. We understand the assignment to require an evidence-based examination of what "integration" has meant operationally across SPREAD's four thematic pillars of peacebuilding, livelihoods, climate resilience and DRR, drawing on community case studies of stronger and weaker integration among pastoralists/agro-pastoralists, fisherfolk, farmers and farmer groups, formal and informal cross-border traders, women- and youth-led CSOs, traditional leaders, local and national authorities, and members of Community Action Groups (CAGs) and Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs). The outputs, a learning paper and two distinct policy briefs, are to inform the European Union, Denmark, IGAD, national governments, and DCA's consortium partners TUPADO, ICPDO, ROG and ECC on which components of integrated programming warrant integration and which can be coordinated separately. Cortech's relevant track record includes the Research and Learning assignment for the Pathway to Prosperity Programme in Turkana West, Kenya, for the Danish Refugee Council (2025), which combined quantitative surveys with KIIs, FGDs and case studies in a fragile pastoralist economy directly adjacent to this assignment's geography. Our consultancy for CEWARN and the IGAD Secretariat (2024) to develop a Regional Strategy Framework integrating climate security into national peace and security policies spanned Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, South Sudan and Uganda, and demonstrates our capacity for multi-country policy translation for IGAD and government audiences of the kind this assignment requires. Our endline evaluation of the climate resilience and peacebuilding project for Lutheran World Federation in Somalia (2026) applied systems-thinking across education, livelihoods, WASH and peacebuilding as interconnected rather than siloed interventions, the same integration logic this learning paper must document for SPREAD. The proposed Lead Consultant/Researcher, Mugove Kwashirai Chakurira, is available for the full assignment period and will lead the desk review, case-study design, learning paper and both policy briefs. Field data collection will be supported by Research Assistant/Enumerator Edwin Aldrin Adenya, consistent with the Terms of Reference requirement that the consultant recruit and train enumerators for community-level engagement. Cortech confirms compliance with the submission requirements of Section A.5 and the Application Process of Annex 1, including the suitability statement, technical proposal, work-plan and financial proposal within the stipulated page limits, the Proposal Submission Form (Annex 2), and certification of compliance with the Code of Conduct for Contractors (Annex 5) and eligibility under Article 33 of the General Terms and Conditions. We remain available to DanChurchAid Kenya for any clarification required prior to the closing date of 24 September 2026, 17:00 hours EAT.

Sampling and Selection Logic

This assignment does not call for a probability sample. The Terms of Reference request community case studies, stronger and weaker examples of integration, and direct engagement with community members, leaders and local authorities rather than population-representative estimates, so Cortech will apply purposive selection throughout. Case-study sites in South Omo, Turkana and Eastern Equatoria will be selected jointly with TUPADO, ICPDO, ROG and ECC against explicit criteria set out in the inception report, including strength of observed integration (drawing on the 2025 Mid-Term Review and reflection workshop outputs), presence of CAGs, VSLAs and CMDRR structures, and coverage of livestock, fishing, farming and formal/informal cross-border trade (ICBT) livelihoods. Within each site, KII and FGD participants will be purposively drawn to represent CAG and VSLA members, traditional leaders, local/national authorities, market committee members, women- and youth-led CSOs, and both women/youth-led and mixed markets, with quota-based attention to sex, age and disability so that disaggregation is possible at the analysis stage rather than assumed at the sampling stage. This logic privileges information richness and contrast between stronger and weaker integration cases over statistical generalisability, consistent with a learning paper rather than a population-based evaluation. SECTION 2. DATA ANALYSIS PLAN

Quantitative inputs generated through the assignment, principally participatory ranking exercise scores and any structured indicators drawn from CAG, VSLA and market committee records, will be cleaned, coded and entered into SPSS. Analysis will be primarily descriptive, using frequencies and cross-tabulations to compare ranking patterns across South Omo, Turkana and Eastern Equatoria and across stronger versus weaker integration case-study sites, disaggregated by sex, age and disability as specified in the ToR. Where sample sizes and data structure allow, Cortech will apply non-parametric tests (for example chi-square comparisons) to assess whether differences in perceived integration value between sites are more than incidental, always reporting these results with appropriate caution given the case-study, non-probability design. Qualitative data from KIIs, FGDs and Outcome Harvesting-informed reflection sessions will be transcribed, cleaned and coded in NVivo using a coding framework built directly from the six proposed learning questions and the six assignment objectives, with dedicated nodes for CAG, VSLA, CMDRR and observatory-platform experience, sequencing choices, and trade-offs between livelihoods and climate resilience/adaptation. Thematic analysis will proceed by first-cycle descriptive coding, followed by pattern coding to surface convergence and divergence between stronger and weaker integration cases and across the three consortium partner geographies.
